orders: Palpate radial and ulnar pulses in the affected arm
Assess capillary refill time in the fingertips of the affected hand
Test pinprick sensation in the median, ulnar, and radial nerve distributions of the hand
Test motor function of the intrinsic hand muscles (abduction/adduction of fingers, opposition of thumb)
X-ray of the affected forearm and wrist
Doppler arterial study of the affected upper extremity
Nerve conduction studies of the upper extremity

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Graves' disease (autoimmune hyperthyroidism from TSH-receptor stimulating antibodies) with Graves' ophthalmopathy

1. Factitious disorder imposed on self (Münchausen syndrome) – chronic arm bandaging without recent trauma and dramatic presentation
2. Other cause of bilateral proptosis (e.g., orbital pseudotumor, idiopathic orbital inflammation, or carotid-cavernous fistula)
3. Sympathomimetic drug intoxication (e.g., cocaine, amphetamines) causing bilateral lid retraction/mydriasis
